themes.title: Investment AI is becoming an information-infrastructure business
themes.thesis: The strongest investment-firm cases position differentiated information access, source quality, permissions, and freshness as core AI infrastructure. The emerging distinction is between answering from a document collection and maintaining a usable view of the firm's changing knowledge.

firmExamples.classification: Investment-firm practitioner; the permissions session is co-presented with infrastructure vendor turbopuffer
firmExamples.maturity: Production explicitly reported in the abstract
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The Vault centralizes internal and external unstructured information and supports PAT, described as used daily by hundreds of investors. The permissions co-presentation describes enforcing complex user-level access at retrieval rather than relying on application-layer checks. A next-generation Researcher is described as being enabled by this platform; its deployment scale is not established.

firmExamples.maturity: Implemented enterprise-state example described; production rollout and measured effectiveness are not specified
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract describes estimating enterprise state from messages, decks, meetings, and other noisy observations. It proposes tracking belief freshness and contradictions, arguing that finding an old statement differs from estimating what is currently true.

themes.learning: The advertised cases suggest that enterprise knowledge must be treated as an operated product: someone owns content quality, access rules, entity meaning, source/version history, and freshness. A stronger model cannot substitute for access to an authoritative source or resolve conflicting firm definitions by itself. Retrieval and state estimation should be compared according to the question being answered, rather than treated as interchangeable architectures.
tips: Separate three questions in a team readout: Can the system find the evidence? May this user see it? Is it still authoritative for this decision? Show how each is tested.
For a research output, retain the source version and the effective date of the fact, not only the URL or the time the agent retrieved it.
Compare document Q&A with a state-estimation approach on a case involving changing or contradictory information before accepting a broader 'world model' claim.
themes.whatNotToConclude: Bridgewater's reported adoption does not prove investment outperformance, and Citadel Securities' proposed framing does not establish that ordinary retrieval is obsolete. Neither case establishes the same requirements for every wealth-management firm.
themes.questionToValidate: Which source-quality, entitlement, and freshness failures still occur in production, and what evidence shows the chosen architecture reduces them?

themes.title: Advisor and analyst AI is becoming part of the workflow
themes.thesis: Public wealth-management disclosures point to knowledge access, meeting preparation, documentation, and follow-up as practical advisor workflows. The conference extends that discussion into persistent financial cases involving several people, tools, and days of work. These are different levels of delegation and require separate evidence.

firmExamples.classification: Financial/wealth-workflow builder presenting its own runtime; do not infer affiliation with another similarly named firm
firmExamples.maturity: Runtime implementation described; client scale, deployment duration, and independently measured automation level are not specified
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract distinguishes continuously running agents from financial work spanning weeks, several agents and humans, and external systems. It advertises orchestration, context, sandboxes, signals, and human involvement when work cannot progress. Its broad automation language remains the speaker's claim.

firmExamples.classification: Agent vendor speaking from claimed production experience in finance workflows
firmExamples.maturity: Production experience claimed; named financial customers and comparable outcome measures are not supplied
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The session describes analysts collaborating in group conversations, working in Office artifacts, and requiring the right context from large deal workspaces. It promises a distinction between workflows ready for delegation and those still requiring a human copilot.

themes.learning: A useful wealth or research assistant fits the work already performed by advisors and analysts: prepare, find evidence, collaborate, document, and follow through. For a case spanning days or weeks, the system also needs an explicit state, an accountable owner, and a reliable handoff. A polished answer alone does not establish that the client or investment workflow was completed well.
tips: Choose the workflow unit carefully: a prepared meeting, an accepted research memo, or a completed service case. Evaluate completion and correction effort, not just answer fluency.
For meeting and client-context tools, ask how consent, sensitive information, CRM writeback, and advisor review work. Retain who approved the final client communication.
For persistent cases, capture state, evidence requirements, accountable owners, escalation conditions, and how interrupted or duplicated work resumes.
themes.whatNotToConclude: These abstracts do not demonstrate fully autonomous wealth advice, universal suitability for client-facing decisions, or elimination of human accountability. The named wealth-specific evidence is narrower than the broader bank and investment-firm coverage.
themes.questionToValidate: Which workflow stages are demonstrably delegated today, which still require people, and what happens when a case stalls or its facts change mid-process?

themes.title: Model choice is one layer of a larger capability system
themes.thesis: Firms appear to be combining frontier models, task-specific context, tools, harnesses, and—in some cases—domain-trained models. The common lesson is to measure the complete capability stack on its intended task, while preserving room for specialized modeling when proprietary data justifies it.

firmExamples.maturity: Production accounting agent and end-to-end benchmark explicitly described
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Ramp advertises ablation experiments showing that added context can hurt performance. It describes reducing a frequently loaded skill and preserving reusable process in memory rather than stale facts from a previous task. The benchmark covers models, tools, skills, memory, and harness together.

firmExamples.maturity: Large-scale transaction-model development and transition toward production described; the abstract does not identify which applications are live
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The session covers representing and tokenizing transaction data, dataset curation, training/evaluation pipelines, adaptive fine-tuning, and multi-task learning for fraud and transaction decisioning. This is a different AI category from an LLM research assistant.

firmExamples.maturity: Broad daily agent use and an operating model are explicitly reported
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Optiver describes task-specific certification exams, routing to the cheapest certified model, and multiple provider/self-hosted channels. Its approach treats model selection as a repeatable capability-and-price decision rather than a one-time vendor choice.

firmExamples.classification: Finance-agent vendor and benchmark collaborator; hedge-fund customer use is vendor-reported
firmExamples.maturity: Benchmark launch plus production-client claims; institutional clients are unnamed in the abstract
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The session attributes large performance differences to harness design and describes point-in-time investment-origination evaluation. The quoted scores and improvements require inspection of the task set, baselines, and scoring methodology.

themes.learning: The advertised approaches support a layered capability view: model, data representation, retrieved context, tools, execution environment, and evaluation. Improving one layer can worsen another, and a benchmark result from coding or banking transactions cannot be assumed to transfer to investment research. A useful industry comparison therefore asks what workload each firm optimized and which variables it held constant.
tips: Compare candidate systems on the same representative workload and record quality, critical failures, latency, cost, and reviewer effort together.
Run ablations on context, memory, and tools before crediting a model upgrade with the entire improvement.
Distinguish LLM assistants from transaction or tabular foundation models in a team report; their data, objectives, validation, and deployment constraints differ.
themes.whatNotToConclude: The cases do not show that foundation-model choice is irrelevant, that every bank should train its own model, or that a vendor's finance benchmark establishes live investment performance.
themes.questionToValidate: After controlling for workload and the surrounding system, which capability gains came from the model, domain data, context, tools, and harness respectively?

themes.title: Reasoning and authority are separating into distinct layers
themes.thesis: The most concrete control stories separate an agent's proposal from permission to execute it, and move repeatable protections into identity, policy, data, and transaction infrastructure. Human review remains valuable for judgment and exceptions, while deterministic controls handle clearly specified limits.

firmExamples.maturity: A built platform/control architecture is described; coverage and effectiveness measures are not supplied
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Wise's LOOP framework is advertised as converting repeated oversight decisions into versioned policies enforced by the platform, with people involved when judgment is needed. The abstract explicitly separates model reasoning from authority over customer funds.

firmExamples.maturity: Technical approaches described as used and effective internally; detailed mechanisms await the talk
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The keynote addresses balancing useful research/engineering agents with safety and operating cost. The abstract supports a practitioner perspective on the tradeoff but does not yet disclose enough detail to prescribe a particular control architecture.

firmExamples.classification: Bank security practitioner participating in a vendor/protocol panel
firmExamples.maturity: Protocol and design discussion; bank production adoption is not established
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The panel asks whether permission to call a tool is sufficient and explores authorization tied to the agent's mission or intent. JPMC speaker participation should not be represented as endorsement or deployment of the named protocol.

firmExamples.maturity: Security analysis and defenses; no specific Bloomberg deployment is established by the abstract
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The keynote addresses prompt injection, data leakage, agent and supply-chain risks. It supplies a security perspective for evaluating an agent architecture; the speaker’s employer does not establish that every technique described is deployed there.

themes.learning: The advertised control patterns suggest a useful distinction between judgment and enforcement. A probabilistic model may identify a proposed action, while enforceable policy defines the allowable resources, identity, budget, and approval conditions. A successful API call or settlement is therefore an operational fact, not evidence that the business action was appropriate.
tips: Draw the authority path alongside the data path: who requested the work, whose permissions apply, what may execute, and where the decision is enforced.
Test denied cases, stale credentials, duplicate actions, retries, and resource mismatches; a happy-path demo is insufficient evidence of control.
Ask which decisions were automated as preventive policy and which remain human judgment; record exception handling and accountability explicitly.
themes.whatNotToConclude: A protocol demonstration does not establish bank adoption, deterministic controls do not remove all model risk, and the presence of human approval does not by itself prove effective oversight.
themes.questionToValidate: Which actions can a compromised or mistaken agent still cause, and what measured evidence shows the control boundaries hold under adversarial and ordinary failures?

themes.title: Evaluation is moving from a score to an operating discipline
themes.thesis: Practitioners are describing evaluation as a continuing process of human calibration, representative cases, failure diagnosis, release gates, and production observation. They are also exposing a second-order problem: the automated evaluator must itself be validated.

firmExamples.maturity: High-volume voice-agent production explicitly reported; automated self-improvement loops are described as being built toward
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract describes a progression from manually reviewing all calls to judges that had to match human graders before running unsupervised. It promises the practical failures and infrastructure behind that transition. The future self-healing ambition must be distinguished from the current operating state.

firmExamples.maturity: Production accounting agent with an existing development/evaluation loop described
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Ramp evaluates complete accounting workflows and compares changes using quality, reliability, latency, and cost rather than a single local metric. Its context-ablation examples offer a practitioner counterpart to the voice-agent calibration case.

firmExamples.firm: Unnamed top global bank, described by Langfuse
firmExamples.classification: Vendor-reported customer pattern; not a named bank practitioner presentation
firmExamples.maturity: A bank deployment-gate pattern is claimed; customer identity, coverage, and independent outcomes are unavailable
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract advertises golden datasets, domain evaluators, a pass/fail gate, and reviewable traces and scores. It can illustrate an evaluation architecture but cannot support a claim about adoption by a specific leading bank.

firmExamples.maturity: Behavior-spec and trajectory-judging approach described as developed; outcome improvement is not quantified
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Basis distinguishes a correct outcome from acceptable intermediate behavior and proposes evaluating both. This complements final-answer evaluation with process evidence on long-horizon research tasks.

themes.learning: The advertised cases suggest that an evaluation result earns the right to support a particular decision only when its task coverage, human agreement, failure sensitivity, and uncertainty are understood. Release evidence and post-release monitoring serve different purposes. Outcome scores, trajectory checks, and human review should be compared as complementary sources of assurance.
tips: Record what a score is allowed to decide: choose a model, ship a change, reduce review, or expand autonomy. These decisions require different evidence.
Calibrate automated judges against independently reviewed examples, including important false passes and disagreements, before increasing reliance on them.
Keep a versioned record of the task set, rubric, evaluator, model, tools, and runtime so changes can be reproduced and regressions diagnosed.
themes.whatNotToConclude: The words 'self-healing' and 'deployment gate' do not establish autonomous remediation at scale. A high average score does not demonstrate safety on critical failures, and a named vendor's bank example is not a named institution's public endorsement.
themes.questionToValidate: What evidence was required to reduce human review, what failures still escape, and how is drift in the automated evaluator detected?

themes.title: The business case is shifting from adoption to attributable outcomes
themes.thesis: Investment and financial firms are advertising a stronger connection between AI work and investment-process utility, operating margin, or reliable engineering output. The useful distinction is between usage, productivity, and causal business impact.

firmExamples.maturity: Daily-use research workflows and implemented measurement process explicitly reported
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Contour describes logging AI-generated ideas with sources and reasoning, tracking which reach portfolio managers and become positions, and comparing performance with benchmarks. For softer signals it proposes comparison with the previous production method and time/signal measures. This is a measurement approach, not independently established causal alpha.

firmExamples.maturity: Portfolio deployment case studies and an operating measurement approach advertised; case-level results await evidence
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract ties AI assessment to diligence, operating deployment, centralized capabilities, partner selection, and operating margin. Its examples span portfolio businesses rather than one uniform financial-adviser workflow.

firmExamples.maturity: Broad daily internal engineering use and model-routing operating approach reported
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Task certification, lower-cost qualifying models, and telemetry are presented as operating mechanisms. The session also promises lessons about where inference spending concentrates and which assumed cost savings failed to materialize.

firmExamples.maturity: Scaled in-house agent use explicitly reported
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The abstract reports Agent Chip's daily task volume and share of merged pull requests. These are useful adoption/output measures but do not, by themselves, establish avoided labor cost, higher code quality, or improved financial outcomes.

themes.learning: The advertised cases support a measurement ladder: people use the system; the system completes useful work; that work improves a process; the process contributes to a business outcome. Each step needs its own evidence. Investment returns have many drivers, while engineering outputs can create downstream review and maintenance costs, so neither more ideas nor more pull requests is a sufficient ROI claim.
tips: Report adoption, quality, efficiency, and financial outcome separately, with the source and limitations of each measure.
Define the counterfactual: what work would have happened without AI, with which cost, quality, and timing? Include review, retries, and rework.
Preserve timestamps and decision lineage for AI-generated investment ideas so later selection and performance are not reconstructed with hindsight.
themes.whatNotToConclude: Tracked positions and benchmark comparisons do not alone establish causal alpha. Adoption statistics are not ROI, and portfolio operating-margin examples do not generalize automatically to wealth management or research organizations.
themes.questionToValidate: Which reported benefits survive a credible baseline, full operating costs, selection effects, and the other factors influencing the business outcome?

themes.title: Scaled adoption pairs a supported path with disciplined experimentation
themes.thesis: Banks and trading firms describe adoption through familiar work channels, shared runtimes, secure tooling, and controlled experiments rather than distributing an assistant license alone. A recurring pattern is to make the approved path convenient while requiring visibility and an exit decision for experiments.

firmExamples.maturity: Current in-house deployment and broad staff use explicitly reported
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Agent Chip is presented as a sandboxed agent using an MCP gateway and orchestration system, integrated with Slack for technical and nontechnical staff. The advertised lesson combines distribution, common infrastructure, and security/observability constraints.

firmExamples.maturity: Current supported path and experiment operating model described
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Optiver advertises a supported golden path plus an experimental funnel that must emit telemetry and either graduate or end. It also describes task-based model certification and multiple provider channels.

firmExamples.classification: Bank/fintech practitioner discussing its internal stack with Together AI
firmExamples.maturity: Current internal coding and vision-model use described; detailed effectiveness and control evidence are not given
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The talk promises experience with written-request-to-code and mockup-to-interface systems in an audited environment. It is a focused account of internal engineering capabilities, not evidence of autonomous customer banking.

firmExamples.maturity: A principles talk; the abstract does not establish a specific deployed agent architecture
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The keynote frames code-quality and review decisions as questions needing durable principles amid competing automation approaches. It can enrich the governance discussion but supplies no adoption or productivity result in advance.

themes.learning: The announced cases suggest that internal platform and product decisions jointly shape adoption. Familiar channels reduce friction, while shared sandboxes, gateways, permissions, and evaluation practices make behavior easier to support. An experiment funnel also needs criteria for promotion and retirement; otherwise a growing collection of agents can become a maintenance portfolio without a clear owner.
tips: Compare the employee journey as well as the model: discovery, access, task submission, result review, escalation, and support.
For each experiment, name an owner, a telemetry contract, a graduation test, and a date or condition for ending it.
Measure successful work and review effort alongside adoption; high task volume can coexist with weak output quality or support burden.
themes.whatNotToConclude: Slack integration is not universally the right interface, a golden path should not imply one model for every task, and these selected success-oriented talks do not establish industry-wide adoption or productivity rates.
themes.questionToValidate: Which shared platform services actually removed adoption barriers, and which experiments failed to graduate or were retired?

themes.title: AI modernization still depends on domain experts and system invariants
themes.thesis: Financial-system modernization is being described as a combination of AI assistance, recovered institutional knowledge, careful migration structure, and explicit validation. The durable industry lesson may be that faster code generation increases the value of knowing which business behaviors cannot change.

firmExamples.maturity: Production ledger migration while legacy systems remained live explicitly described
firmExamples.reportedPattern: Vanguard describes separate producer migration, gold-copy replication, and consumer migration tracks; CDC-based synchronization; database-layer idempotency; and decoupled consumer access. AI tools are described as helping maintain two codebases. The abstract does not attribute the entire modernization outcome to AI.

firmExamples.classification: Insurance practitioner describing an enterprise experiment with a model provider
firmExamples.maturity: Explicitly an experiment; replication across teams is described as an adaptable methodology rather than established firm-wide scale
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The war-room approach assembles a small team, on-call technical/product/business experts, tools, system context, and a curated playbook. The abstract reports a first-day annualized saving; its calculation, implementation status, and durability need validation.

firmExamples.classification: Two vendors presenting financial-firm implementation patterns; customers are not named in the abstract
firmExamples.maturity: Large-financial-firm implementations claimed; customer verification and comparable outcomes are not available
firmExamples.reportedPattern: The session advertises using a knowledge graph and agents to reconstruct legacy business rules and dependencies, then plan and validate modernization with guardrails and human approval. Reported acceleration remains a vendor claim until the supporting cases are examined.

themes.learning: The announced cases suggest that domain knowledge and validation are the scarce inputs in modernization. Vanguard's migration design protects financial consistency; GEICO's experts and playbook supply knowledge that the model does not possess; the vendor graph case seeks to recover hidden dependencies. The team should distinguish proven migration engineering from the incremental contribution of AI.
tips: Record the nonnegotiable invariants—transaction completeness, reconciliation, idempotency, permissions, and downstream behavior—before discussing code-generation speed.
Ask how system experts contribute knowledge, resolve ambiguity, and approve consequential decisions; capture that process as carefully as the tools.
Separate measured AI contribution from the total project's benefits and separate annualized potential savings from realized recurring savings.
themes.whatNotToConclude: An annualized saving from an experiment does not establish realized enterprise ROI. A successful ledger migration does not prove AI can replace migration controls, and unnamed vendor customer claims should not be attributed to a particular financial institution.
themes.questionToValidate: Which parts of the result required AI, which depended on established migration controls and expert knowledge, and what independently checked outcome persisted after the experiment?

tips: Make every financial number traceable

Retain the entity, period, units, currency, source version, and calculation path. A correct citation can still point to the wrong period or denominator. Distinguish sourced figures from calculated results and forecasts.
Separate agent recall from human-facing usefulness

Scope the time period and decision, then evaluate retrieval coverage separately from final-brief relevance and noise. A shared repository does not require identical retrieval or presentation for people and agents.
Evaluate the work product people accept

For research, measure an accepted memo or useful signal. For advisors, measure a prepared meeting or accurate follow-up. Include the human corrections needed before use; a completed model response is only one step.
ae273f0b-db0f-4638-8ae3-05874bebf9ca
Evaluate skill and memory changes on complete jobs

Define tasks and accepted completion before comparing bundles. Keep partial credit separate from binary pass criteria, and state the attempt budget and output-selection costs behind pass@k. Eight-to-four skills is an experiment, not a universal default.
Calibrate judges as configured system components

Keep safety, task, and experience measures separate. Version the judge model and rubric; measure severe false passes, false failures, disagreement, and repeated-run variance. A fail-leaning judge can increase review burden.
Test the consequential failure path

Seek disconfirming cases. Test containment, detection, and human intervention alongside output quality; preserve found failures as regression cases and verify repairs on a separate assessment set. Frequency alone does not describe risk.
Connect the registry to enforced boundaries
Record owners, tools, endpoints, and resources, then test allowed and denied actions. For selective approval, measure missed consequential cases as well as unnecessary interruptions.
73badd10-6f8c-4c95-b5e7-55fc3d7bafc1
Package domain judgment into reviewed skills

Use Range’s recorded Pick–Teach–Pack–Test–Ship sequence to expose inputs, why, required questions, and limits. Test accepted analysis quality and correction effort; parallel drafting does not by itself establish autonomous advice or capacity gains.
Compare cost per accepted task

Include inference, retries, tools, review, rework, support, and maintenance. Choose lower-cost models only after they meet the relevant task and critical-failure requirements. Keep cost estimates separate from realized savings.
Give experiments an exit decision

Name an owner, required telemetry, graduation criteria, and a retirement condition. The supported path should make common work convenient while experiments generate evidence about whether they deserve ongoing support.
58fe4b11-571e-4afd-bd89-8ad63e6cfe11
Separate maintainability from immediate consequence
Ask who depends on a tool and how long it must live. Rapid replacement may justify less long-term maintenance, while a wrong financial result or sensitive-data exposure can still matter immediately.
Make traces usable for verified improvement
Connect request context, actions, evidence, outcomes, and evaluation results. An automated diagnosis is a hypothesis: reproduce the issue, assess a fix, and retain an accountable release decision.
